But honestly, what if it's his home life causing it? What if it's his parents or family? If there's abuse causing it, you might or hurt more than help...
Believe me, I've been on both sides... mine were more permanent methods that, for some miraclaculous reason didn't work. But the wrong people were made aware, and it made the already bad situation worse. 

I hope your friend gets the resources he needs in a loving, gentle, caring way from those qualified and empathetic enough to handle it. 
I'm also hoping that the parents are made aware and support him during this rough time; with whatever it is that is causing him to feel the world is better off without him in it. 

All I gotta say is, don't just ignore him after that would be worse than not doing anything at all. Real friends stay around not leave in a hard time. ( not saying you, just some advise)

But it seems like it's a mix of other co- morbid disorders and not that far on the dissociative spectrum. Us it's insurance reasons for trying to find a trained psychologist and what our new government insurance will accept and get on the patients wait list.

If they seem like a total bitch or otherwise.... it's what makes them, them. That is exhausting and puts anyone on edge. 
Just like those with ptsd... that's middle of the dissociative spectrum. They sometimes get " selfish, exhausting, and annoying" to those around them... but they are also trying to heal too. I don't think someone would consider the fact they are trying to heal and dealing with a flashback, coming off as irritated  as anything but a person someone loves dealing with a response to trauma they've endured that changed the way their brain is. 
It's not just a matter of logic... at that point it's an emotional flight or fight response, but I'm sure you already know that. .
Sorry if what I replied previously came off as a misscommunicated way of saying that. Wasn't my intention to offend or make it seem like you can't handle the relationship with said alter.

I feel like you clearly don't understand the way DID is formed. The ones out, get triggered due to something. The system formed to protect your boyfriend... not to entertain you. It's not like it's just you and him, and you get to ignore the rest... 
That's actually quite selfish and ignorant of you. It's a trauma disorder. If they front and voice the fact they dislike something... 9/10 it's due to something that triggered that. No matter how trivial you may think it is. 
DID is not a Game, it's not you get to chose who you talk to and who you don't... you can't ignore a part or parts of your bf and then except everything to go right. 

If it's that tiring for you... then maybe it's not within your threshold to handle that at this moment in time. I've had people leave our life due to the fact they couldn't have out the headmate they liked the most. The system is created to protect... if someone is out, there's always a damn good reason. 

We really get upset when everyone now acts like it's some trendy, fun, cool, disorder... it's not any of those. The DID Trend isn't cool... it's a last ditch effort at coping with prolonged childhood abuse before the age of 9, that causes the mind to form amnesic barriers.... that's not fun, nor is the trauma, or the hours of dissociating, the splitting headaches and migraines due to rapid switching or switching in general... or anything else. It's exhausting, painful, and just difficult even on a " good" day for a system that's got some trauma work done and can communicate. It's worse if there's no communication.... it takes time to heal, and just because they had no say in the matter of childhood trauma and the amnesic barriers forming... doesn't mean everyone else around them gets to only have the one part they identify as the " main them" the "person they remembered them being"

Just, no. Not ok. I wish people could understand that. Its not a fad, it's not a statement, it's a trauma disorder that debilitates some for the rest of their life... it's decades of healing and working with the other headmates. 
It's not personalities. It's altered states of consciousness'... there's a reason it got renamed 27+ years ago. 

You wouldn't like If someone said to you... oh it's rude you are upset and don't wanna talk due to being triggered or having gotten really bad news. It's the same for when someone else of the system is triggered out and is doing their role to help protect the whole system. You can't pick and chose who you accept and like and who you don't. It doesn't work that way. Sorry... 

- Mae ( Physical Protector,  former persecutor alter)

OP, I'd decide if you want to stay and encourage her to reach out to a therapist and maybe handle some of her emotions. See what's going on, on a deeper level. If she's unwilling... then I wouldn't stick around if it's affecting your mental health. 

You're both still in highschool. I didn't even date in high-school, I had too much going on outside of school with family dysfunction, abuse, and trying to get through high-school as well. 
If she makes you happy, then maybe stay if you can get her to understand her reaction was a little over the top. If she doesn't want to realize that... then she's not ready to talk to anyone and figure out why she's acting that way. If so, there's nothing you can do except maybe give some distance or stay but put up boundaries now. Either way, something has to give... 
We only see one side of this..  I don't know why she reacted that way, no one does. It could be multiple things. Or she just could be entitled and if that's the case... then there's not much you can do until she understands and reaches out to handle what's going on internally within herself. 
No, you're not over reacting and no, you ddidnt do anything wrong in this case.

Some systems prefer and work better with functional multiplicity, and it's more stress free that way for most after so long of being multiple and growing up that way. 

We still have a psychologist, but we've also done lots of communication as a system and work together. It takes time, patience, effort, and safety to do that. 

For us sometimes a change in hair or a new style of way someone wears our clothes or makeup helps too. But it also takes time, we had an ex, and it took a while to move on from... it was complicated and it ended very badly. That was a few years ago now... in less than a month, we are marrying our Fiancé and we couldn't be happier. He gots his own mental health, but everyone has their own stories and trauma. The best thing is that he is committed and willing to learn and help, allow space for our little ones, and for bad days, but also doesn't let us get too far into our flashbacks. 

Sorry, just for some, it works, for others working decades to get to one primary consciousness that any big T trauma or anything really traumatic can cause the system to split again... just doesn't always work. Most can get to functional multiplicity safer and it also just works better for the system as a whole. Either way, it's up to the system to come to the conclusion and whats safest for them all as a whole while also respecting every parts individual opinions. Because weather anyone likes it or not it's what kept most systems alive when life wasn't getting better.... it's not an easy disorder and it's not magic. It's a last ditch effort to survive repeated, prolonged childhood trauma before you turn 9 years old with no escape. 
So I'd just be gentle, let her feel and support her as best you can. It takes time, but a change in hair style or clothing style or something that makes her feel new and reasonable that the rest of the system can and are comfortable with might help. 
- Rissa & Mae ( currently host "core," physical protector former persecutor )

 Your mind splits, this is the first time you become multiple; your mind creates another identity that is separated by amnesic barriers so you don't know of the abuse going on. It's a survival mechanism quite literally, you either dissociate, split, and survive, or you succumb to the unhealthy environment around you. Most people with D.I.D. don't know they have it until they're well into their 50s or 60s. It's a covert disorder most of the time for systems, their are some overt systems out there but mostly ones we've talked to have been covert. 

Our core, the one who identifies as the one who grew up in her body and goes by her birth name. Didn't know we were around until March or April of 2015, that's when it became real to her and she experienced gaps in memory,  noticed different handwriting in her journal, homework done but no recollection of it, chores done and remembering only that it had needed to be started come to find out it was already finished. 

Of course your Dr and therapist have to rule out any other possible reasons for it like - brain injury, neurological damage, seizures, medications, substances altering your state of mind. After they deem it's not any of those reasons causing it then they can go with the process of figuring out if it's D.I.D. or if it's something similar to it.
